subject: Next steps: AcuityHealth residency & routing constraints (post-demo)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acuityhealth.com>, Meera Patel <meera.patel@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo recap + qualification on data residency constraints

Tom / Meera — thanks for your time today. Quick recap from our side and the next steps we discussed: 

- Key constraints you mentioned: patient data must remain in EU datacenters for all PII-derived inference, low-latency APAC access for a small subset of anonymized model calls, and strict audit logs for each inference request.
- Qualification question we need to confirm: do you require a fully air-gapped on-prem deployment for any part of the pipeline, or is a VPC/private deployment with customer-controlled KMS acceptable?
- Short-term options we proposed on the call: (1) Hosted API in EU-only tenancy with strict cross-region egress controls (fastest), (2) Dedicated capacity pinned to EU region with VPC peering and customer KMS, or (3) Private deployment (customer VPC or on-prem) for full control.

Next steps / asks (action items):
1) Meera: please confirm whether any regulatory audits require physical on-prem storage or whether EU-only cloud residency is sufficient.
2) Acuity security team: share a short list of mandatory controls (we can map to SOC2 / encryption / audit logs).
3) Ben / Lauren / I will prepare a short one-pager comparing the three hosting modes focused on EU residency, cross-border routing, and fallback behavior.
4) Sean: offer a technical deep-dive call with infra/ops — available Thursday or Friday this week.

I attached a stub SOC2 summary and a very small VPC diagram we can expand. Will follow up with a recommended pilot configuration after Meera and security send the mandatory controls.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments:
- Redwood_SOC2_summary_v2.pdf (summary, 3 pages)
- vpc_network_diagram_stub.png (stub: recommended peering and egress guards)

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acuityhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Meera Patel <meera.patel@acuityhealth.com>, AcuityHealth Security Team <security@acuityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T18:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + qualification on data residency constraints

Thanks Sean — clear summary. Quick answers from our side: 

- Regulatory must: All PII-derived inference results and the raw input records must not leave the EU. That rules out any solution that routes PII out of-region, even transiently.
- APAC requirement: Our clinical ops team in APAC needs sub-200ms responses for a small set of non-PII inferencing (anonymized telemetry). That could be handled by regional caching or a lightweight APAC model instance.
- On-prem vs VPC: Preference is VPC/private deployment on a customer-controlled subnet (Azure/EU region) with our KMS. On-prem is a last resort due to cost and ops overhead.
- Audit: We need request-level audit logs (request id, model version, timestamp, routing decision) retained for 2 years.

Can you call out whether Dedicated capacity (EU pinned) + VPC peering + customer KMS will meet the non-PHI/PII split without routing any PII outside EU? Also, what are fallback behaviors if EU capacity is saturated — can we fail closed for PII requests while allowing non-PII calls to go to alternative regions?

We can do a follow-up technical session Friday 2026-12-11 at 10:00 CET — Meera and a security engineer will join.

—Tom
Product Ops Lead | AcuityHealth
T: +44 20 7946 0785

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acuityhealth.com>, Meera Patel <meera.patel@acuityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-11T08:35:00Z
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + qualification on data residency constraints

Sean / team — quick internal note (will share with Acuity in the call):

- Dedicated (EU pinned) + customer VPC peering + customer KMS: This satisfies the "PII must not leave EU" requirement provided we enforce strict routing policies in the control plane:
  * All requests tagged as PII are forced to EU-only serving pools (we can add an input classifier or rely on your annotation).
  * KV cache and prefix caching are constrained to EU devices; we can disable cross-region cache replication.
  * Network egress: we support VPC egress rules + egress gateways to guarantee no out-of-region egress for tenant traffic.

- Fallback behavior options (important to document):
  1) Fail-closed for PII: if EU capacity exhausted, return an error for PII calls (recommended for regs).
  2) Queue-and-retry: hold requests for a short window (configurable) while autoscaler tries to add capacity (higher latency).
  3) Emergency fallback to a vetted alt-region with explicit contractual approval (not acceptable for Acuity's PII constraint).

- APAC non-PII handling: two technical approaches: regional cache + lightweight model (fast, minimal data residency impact) or regional read-only replica that only serves anonymized requests. Both preserve EU residency for PII.

Action items for internal prep before Fri 10:00 CET:
- Lauren: prepare a one-page table mapping hosting mode -> residency guarantees -> fallback policy -> SLA impact.
- Sean: consolidate the SOC2 and KMS integration notes; confirm whether HSM-backed keys supported for customer-managed KMS (we do).
- I will pull capacity and autoscaling knobs and estimated warm-up times for Dedicated pools in EU central locations (Frankfurt/Netherlands).

Ben
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@acuityhealth.com>, Meera Patel <meera.patel@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T20:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + qualification on data residency constraints — proposed pilot and materials

Tom / Meera — thanks again. Per our call and the internal notes below, here are the concrete recommendations and proposed next steps so you can circulate to legal/security: 

1) Recommended short pilot configuration (30-day): Dedicated EU-pinned capacity in Azure West Europe + VPC peering into your Azure tenant + customer-managed KMS (HSM-backed supported). All PII-tagged requests are routed only to EU serving pools; cache replication is disabled. Failure mode for PII: fail-closed.

2) APAC low-latency path: lightweight APAC model instance that only holds anonymized, non-PII feature payloads. We will add an input classifier rule so anything with patient identifiers is never sent to APAC.

3) Deliverables we are attaching for initial review: Redwood_SOC2_summary_v2.pdf (compliance mapping), vpc_network_diagram_stub.png (shows peering + egress gateway + audit log flow). We will follow up the SOC2 mapping with a short control-matrix mapping Acuity requirements to Redwood features.

4) Scheduling: Confirming the technical deep-dive Friday 2026-12-11 10:00 CET (we have Ben and Lauren on that call). If that time doesn't work, propose Monday 2026-12-14 09:00 CET.

5) Contract and procurement: If pilot OK, propose a 30-day paid pilot agreement; Lauren will draft a minimal statement of work and a DocuSign template (link below).

DocuSign pilot template: https://app.docusign.com/templates/rs-redwood-acuity-pilot
HubSpot record: https://hubspot.company/contacts/ACCT-78921

Let me know if you want any additional diagrams (network flow, key lifecycle, audit log retention). We can also produce a short runbook describing fail-closed behavior for PII.
